title: Make a missing @add_example() example a hard error (triage ~18 existing offenders first)
description:
## Background

Split out from the fix for posit-dev/py-shiny-site#370 (see py-shiny PR #2369).

`@add_example()` in `shiny/_docstring.py` catches a missing example and merely prints a `::warning`, then returns the docstring unchanged:

```python
except ExampleNotFoundException as e:
    ...
    print(f"::warning file={file},line=...::{fn_name} - {e}")
    return func   # silently skips the example
```

This silent failure is exactly why the `ui.Theme` example went missing on the deployed (Linux) site for a long time without anyone noticing (#370). The existence of the `no_example()` helper — whose docstring is literally "Prevent `@add_example()` from throwing an error about missing examples" — shows the *intended* contract is that a declared-but-missing example should be an **error**. The silent `::warning` is a weakening of that contract.

## Proposal

Make a declared-but-missing example a **hard error** during the docs build (`SHINY_ADD_EXAMPLES=true`), so casing/naming/mode regressions fail loudly instead of silently shipping docs with no example. Functions that legitimately lack an example in a given mode should be annotated with `@no_example(mode)` (the mechanism already exists).

## Blocker: ~18 functions currently rely on the silent warning

Flipping the `except` to `raise` today would break `make quartodoc`. Reproduced by importing shiny with `SHINY_ADD_EXAMPLES=true` in both `SHINY_MODE=core` and `SHINY_MODE=express`. Each needs a per-function decision: add a real example, add `@no_example(mode)`, or remove a stale `@add_example()` decorator.

**Group A — example directory entirely missing (11):** the `@add_example(...)` reference is stale/broken; produces no example on any platform.

- `__call__`
- `close` (`Session.close`, `@add_example("session_close")` — no `api-examples/close/` dir)
- `column`
- `dynamic_route`
- `on_bookmark`
- `on_bookmarked`
- `on_ended`
- `on_flush`
- `on_flushed`
- `send_custom_message`
- `update_navs`

**Group B — dir exists but no example for the express mode (7):** has an `app-core.py` but no express example, so only warns in express mode.

- `card_body`
- `download_link`
- `output_transformer`
- `restore_input`
- `row`
- `showcase_bottom`
- `showcase_left_center`
- `showcase_top_right`

## Tasks

- [ ] Triage each of the 18 functions above (add example / `@no_example(mode)` / remove stale decorator)
- [ ] Change `_docstring.py` so a missing declared example raises instead of warning
- [ ] Confirm `make quartodoc` (both modes) builds clean

## Notes

To reproduce the current warnings:

```bash
SHINY_ADD_EXAMPLES=true SHINY_MODE=core   python -c "import shiny, shiny.express, shiny.ui, shiny.render, shiny.reactive, shiny.session, shiny.types, shiny.express.ui" 2>&1 | grep '::warning'
SHINY_ADD_EXAMPLES=true SHINY_MODE=express python -c "import shiny, shiny.express, shiny.ui, shiny.render, shiny.reactive, shiny.session, shiny.types, shiny.express.ui" 2>&1 | grep '::warning'
```

title: feat: Add `shiny skills` CLI subcommand (list/get bundled agent skills)
description:
Part of #2269. Depends on #2339 (ships the first bundled skill).

Add a `shiny skills` command group to the CLI so users and agents can discover and read Agent Skills bundled in the shiny package — without needing `uvx library-skills`.

## Scope

- `shiny skills list` — enumerate skills shipped under `shiny/.agents/skills/` (name + one-line description from SKILL.md frontmatter).
- `shiny skills get <name>` — print the skill's SKILL.md directly to stdout (same UX as `agent-browser skills get agent-browser` and `{btw}` 1.3.0's `btw skills get ...`).
- Implement as `shiny/_main_skills.py` following the existing `_main_*.py` pattern, registered on the click `main` group in `shiny/_main.py`.
- Helpful errors: unknown skill name lists available skills; empty/missing skills directory says so.

## Out of scope

- Installing/symlinking skills into a project (that's `uvx library-skills`' job).
- Authoring skill content (see #2339).

title: feat: Ship a `debugging` agent skill in the shiny package (.agents/skills)
description:
Part of #2269.

Ship an [Agent Skill](https://library-skills.io/) inside the shiny package bundle that teaches coding agents how to debug and inspect running Shiny apps — centered on test mode and `export_test_values()` from #2269.

## Scope

- Add `shiny/.agents/skills/debugging/SKILL.md` (library-skills convention: skills live under `.agents/skills/` in the shipped package bundle, so `uvx library-skills` can discover and symlink them into a project's `.agents/skills/` or `.claude/skills/`).
- Skill content teaches agents how to:
  - Enable test mode (`SHINY_TESTMODE=1`) and read the `/session/<token>/dataobj/shinytest` snapshot endpoint (`{input, output, export}`).
  - Use `export_test_values()` (module-level and `session.export_test_values(**kwargs)`) to surface internal reactive values, including module namespacing behavior.
  - Use `session.get_test_snapshot_url()`.
  - General debugging actions: `SHINY_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG`, `shiny run --reload`, interpreting serialization-error markers in snapshots.
- Packaging: ensure the dot-directory is included in the wheel/sdist (hatchling may need an explicit include). Add a packaging test that inspects the built wheel so the skill can't silently drop out of the bundle.

## Out of scope

- `shiny skills` CLI subcommand (separate sub-issue).

## Prior art

- R package `{btw}` 1.3.0 ships skills under `inst/skills` with `btw skills get ...`.
- `agent-browser skills get agent-browser`.

title: CI: playwright-shiny shards fail on syrupy "unused snapshots" even when all tests pass
description:
> [!NOTE]
> This issue was researched and written by Claude Code after observing the failure on an unrelated docs-only PR (#2332).

## Summary

`playwright-shiny` CI shards are failing with exit code 1 from syrupy's unused-snapshot check even though **every test in the shard passes**. The failure occurs on `main` (scheduled and push runs) as well as on PRs, and it did **not** recover when the failed jobs were restarted, so this behaves as persistent breakage rather than a pass-on-rerun flake.

## Failure signature

The job log ends like this (all green, then a nonzero exit):

```
--------------------------- snapshot report summary ----------------------------
2 snapshots passed. 10 snapshots unused.
Re-run pytest with --snapshot-update to delete unused snapshots.
==================== 74 passed, 1 rerun in 94.45s (0:01:34) ====================
make[1]: *** [Makefile:234: playwright] Error 1
make: *** [Makefile:244: playwright-shiny] Error 2
##[error]Process completed with exit code 2.
```

Other affected shards show `12 snapshots unused.` with `90 passed` or `79 passed`.

## Affected runs

- PR #2332 (docs-only change), run [28878032396](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/28878032396): `playwright-shiny (3.14, chromium)` shards 0, 1, and 2 failed; shard 3 passed. Restarting the failed jobs reproduced the identical failure ([shard 0 rerun job](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/28878032396/job/85659790185)).
- `main` scheduled run [28854865414](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/28854865414) (2026-07-07): same signature on `playwright-shiny (3.10, chromium, 1)` (`2 snapshots passed. 10 snapshots unused.`, `79 passed`) and `playwright-shiny (3.13, firefox, 2)` (`12 snapshots unused.`, `70 passed, 3 skipped`).
- `main` push run [28814680090](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/28814680090) (merge of #2331) also failed, though that run additionally shows a real single-test failure on webkit.

## Analysis

The snapshot counts point at `tests/playwright/shiny/components/data_frame/example/__snapshots__/test_data_frame.ambr`, which contains exactly **12 snapshots** (matching the `12 unused` / `2 passed + 10 unused` arithmetic). The snapshot assertions live in parametrized tests in `tests/playwright/shiny/components/data_frame/example/test_data_frame.py` (pandas/polars parametrization).

The `playwright-shiny` workflow shards tests with `--num-shards 4 --shard-id N` (`.github/workflows/pytest.yaml`), which can distribute the parametrized test items of a single module across different shards. A shard that runs only some (or none) of the module's snapshot-asserting items sees the remaining `.ambr` entries as "unused", and syrupy fails the session with exit code 1 even though every executed test passed.

## Possible directions

- Make syrupy's unused-snapshot check non-fatal (warning) for sharded CI runs, keeping it strict for unsharded/local runs.
- Keep all test items of snapshot-using modules within a single shard.
- Move/refactor the snapshot assertions so each shard's collected set is self-consistent.

## Staleness

Per `.claude/references/commit-conventions.md`: close if no new occurrences are reported for 30 days (though note this one currently reproduces deterministically, so it likely needs a fix rather than aging out).

title: feat: Add `render.download_button` and `render.download_link`
description:
### Motivation

In Express, `@render.download` automatically renders its UI, and `download.auto_output_ui()` hard-codes `ui.download_button()`. There is no Express-native way to produce a download *link*. Today you have to reach into Core UI and suppress the auto-rendered button:

```python
from shiny.express import render, ui
from shiny.ui import download_link

download_link("downloadData", "Download")

# `ui.hold()` suppresses the auto-rendered download *button* so the link above is used.
with ui.hold():

    @render.download(filename="data.csv")
    async def downloadData(): ...
```

(This is what `shiny/api-examples/download_link/app-express.py` has to do.)

### Proposal

Add `render.download_button` and `render.download_link`, which differ only in their Express auto-generated UI:

- `render.download_button.auto_output_ui()` → `ui.download_button()`
- `render.download_link.auto_output_ui()` → `ui.download_link()`

In Core they would behave identically to `render.download` (like `render.text` vs `render.code`, the docs would pair `render.download_button` with `ui.download_button()` and `render.download_link` with `ui.download_link()`).

The Express example then becomes:

```python
from shiny.express import render


@render.download_link(filename="data.csv", label="Download")
async def downloadData(): ...
```

### Precedent: 1:1 pairing of renderers and output components

This follows the same reasoning as #997, which split `render.text()` / `render.code()` specifically so each renderer maps 1:1 to its own output component in Express (`ui.output_text()` vs `ui.output_text_verbatim()`, later `ui.output_code()`), while remaining interchangeable in Core.

### Open questions

- Should `render.download` remain as an alias for `render.download_button`, or eventually be deprecated in favor of the two explicit variants?
- Both renderers should presumably keep the existing `label` argument (and this may be a natural place to address the styling flexibility requested in #1230, e.g. an `icon` or `class_` pass-through to the UI function).

### Related

- #997 — Add `render.code()` (establishes the 1:1 renderer ↔ output component pattern)
- #1230 — Allow user to change `render.download` button style
- #971 — Consider replacing `output_args()` (philosophy for customizing render-generated output UI)

title: refactor: Migrate remaining ex_dir= call sites to add_example(example_name=)
description:
Follow-up to #2278, which added an `example_name=` parameter to `@add_example()` (`shiny/_docstring.py`).

`example_name="foo"` finds the nearest `api-examples/` directory by walking up from the decorated object's source file (same mechanism as the no-argument form) and looks up the `foo` subdirectory. This replaces `ex_dir="../api-examples/foo"`, which hardcodes a path relative to the source file and breaks silently-fragile ways when a module moves or the `../` depth is miscounted (e.g. `shiny/render/_data_frame_utils/` needs `../../`, `shiny/ui/_chat.py` needs `../shiny/`).

#2278 migrated the 9 call sites it introduced (`shiny/session/_session.py`, `shiny/bookmark/_bookmark.py`). **37 pre-existing `ex_dir=` call sites remain** across:

- `shiny/express/_module.py`
- `shiny/module.py`
- `shiny/render/_data_frame.py`
- `shiny/render/_data_frame_utils/_datagridtable.py`
- `shiny/render/_express.py`
- `shiny/render/_render.py`
- `shiny/types.py`
- `shiny/ui/_bootstrap.py`
- `shiny/ui/_chat.py`
- `shiny/ui/_input_task_button.py`
- `shiny/ui/_input_update.py`
- `shiny/ui/_markdown_stream.py`
- `shiny/ui/_modal.py`
- `shiny/ui/_offcanvas.py`
- `shiny/ui/_output.py`
- `shiny/ui/busy_indicators.py`
- `shiny/ui/dataframe/_data_frame.py`

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. All `ex_dir="../..."` relative-path call sites use `example_name=` instead (keep `ex_dir=` only if a site genuinely needs a directory outside the nearest `api-examples/` tree).
2. Verify example resolution in both modes: `SHINY_ADD_EXAMPLES=true SHINY_MODE=core python -c "import shiny, shiny.express"` and the same with `SHINY_MODE=express` (missing examples now raise, per #2278).
3. `make docs-quartodoc` builds cleanly.
4. Consider deprecating or documenting-away `ex_dir=` if no call sites remain.

title: [Bug]: value_box() docstring for id gives wrong reactive-value syntax (input.<id>()["full_screen"] instead of input.<id>_full_screen())
description:
### Component

Documentation

### Severity

P3 - Low (minor inconvenience)

### Shiny Version

1.6.4.dev3

### Python Version

3.11

### Minimal Reproducible Example

```python
from shiny.express import ui, render, input

  with ui.value_box(id="churn_box", full_screen=True):
      "Churn Rate"
      "3.4%"

      @render.text
      def churn_detail():
          # Docstring-recommended syntax — silently never updates
          if input.churn_box() and input.churn_box()["full_screen"]:
              return "Expanded"
          return "Collapsed"

  # Clicking the expand icon never changes churn_detail's text, and no error is surfaced in the UI — it just silently does nothing, which makes the bug easy to miss.
```

### Behavior

  Suggested fix

  Update the id parameter docstring in value_box() (_valuebox.py:373-375) to match card()'s wording:

  id
      Provide a unique identifier for the :func:`~shiny.ui.value_box()` to report its
      state to Shiny. For example, using `id="my_value_box"`, you can observe the
      value box's full screen state with `input.my_value_box_full_screen()`.


### Error Messages (if any)

```shell
the code itself works correctly (value_box()'s full_screen behavior functions as designed); the bug is purely that the docstring for the id parameter describes the wrong
  reactive-value syntax.
```

### Environment

```markdown
Mac OS 26.5.1 (25F80)
Chrome 149
```

title: fix(tests): Trim app-boot cost in test_shiny_create and test_external_templates
description:
Part of #2308.

Template-based example tests each create and boot a full app, costing 8–20s per test (run [28639206793](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/28639206793)):

- `tests/playwright/examples/test_shiny_create.py` — `dashboard-tips` (14–20s), `basic-navigation`, `basic-sidebar`, `dashboard` (12–16s each); each test runs `shiny create` then boots the generated app
- `tests/playwright/examples/test_external_templates.py` — `stock-app`, `regularization`, `model-scoring`, `dashboard-tips`, `nba-dashboard` at 8–14s each

Also in the same tier: `tests/playwright/examples/test_examples.py` for `busy_indicators` (13s) and `model-score` (12s), and `tests/playwright/ai_generated_apps/core_express/navset_pill/test_navset_pill_core_express.py::test_navset_pill_demo` at 12–13s per app variant.

Much of this is inherent (template scaffolding + app boot + data/plot rendering), so the goal is to trim overhead and confirm sharding spreads these evenly rather than to make them fast.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. Identify avoidable overhead (e.g. repeated `shiny create` scaffolding, redundant browser navigation, fixed waits)
2. Confirm the pytest-split shards distribute these slow example tests evenly, or improve the split

title: fix(tests): Reduce 12-13s app-startup (setup phase) time in Playwright test apps
description:
Part of #2308.

Several Playwright tests spend **12–13s in the pytest `setup` phase** — the Shiny app process booting and importing heavy libraries (pandas, plotting) before the browser even connects (run [28639206793](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/28639206793)):

- `tests/playwright/shiny/components/data_frame/df_methods/test_df_methods.py::test_dataframe_methods`
- `tests/playwright/shiny/components/data_frame/example/test_data_frame.py::test_single_selection`
- `tests/playwright/shiny/components/busy_indicators/test_busy_indicators.py::test_busy_indicators`

**Ideas to explore:**
- Trim heavy imports / data loading in the test apps (smaller datasets, lazy imports)
- Check whether the local-app fixture has a fixed startup wait vs. polling for readiness
- Share an app fixture across tests in the same file where isolation permits

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. Setup phase for these tests reduced well below 10s, or the cost explained as irreducible

title: fix(tests): Reduce data frame Playwright test durations
description:
Part of #2308.

Several data frame Playwright tests run 15–18s each (run [28639206793](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/28639206793)):

- `tests/playwright/shiny/components/data_frame/html_columns/test_html_columns.py::test_validate_html_columns` — ~18s each for the pandas and polars variants
- `tests/playwright/shiny/components/data_frame/row_selection/test_row_selection.py::test_row_selection` — 16s webkit
- `tests/playwright/shiny/components/data_frame/df_methods/test_df_methods.py::test_dataframe_methods` — 15s call (plus a 13s setup, tracked in #2314)

Worth checking for large rendered tables where a smaller dataset would exercise the same code paths, and for repeated full-table expectations that each wait on re-renders.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. Identify why these specific data frame tests are 10× slower than typical tests
2. Reduce their runtime while keeping coverage of HTML columns, row selection, and df methods

title: fix(tests): Investigate 22-25s runtime of test_inputs_update
description:
Part of #2308.

`tests/playwright/shiny/inputs/test_inputs_update.py::test_updates` takes **25s on chromium and 22s on webkit** (run [28639206793](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/28639206793)).

This is a kitchen-sink test exercising `update_*` functions across many input widgets in one test body. Worth checking for sequential waits that could overlap, redundant expectations, or slider-drag steps (see #2311).

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. Identify the dominant time sinks within the test
2. Reduce runtime (or split into parallelizable tests) without losing update-function coverage

title: fix(tests): Reduce slider drag-simulation cost in input_slider test suites
description:
Part of #2308.

Slider tests are the largest cumulative Playwright cost in CI (run [28639206793](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/28639206793)):

- `tests/playwright/shiny/inputs/test_input_slider.py::test_input_slider_kitchen` — **37s chromium / 31s webkit**
- `tests/playwright/shiny/inputs/input_slider/test_input_slider_app.py` — every test takes 14–20s (`test_slider_range`, `test_slider_loop`, `test_slider_date_format`, `test_slider_drag_range_disabled`, `test_slider_custom_format`), totaling **~80–90s per browser** for the file

The cost comes from drag simulation: each slider move is performed as many small mouse-move events with waits in the controller's drag helpers.

**Ideas to explore:**
- Fewer intermediate mouse-move steps in the `InputSlider` controller drag logic
- Set slider values via keyboard (arrow keys / Home / End) where drag mechanics aren't the behavior under test
- Trim redundant value assertions per drag

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. Cumulative slider test time reduced meaningfully (target: at least halved)
2. Drag interaction itself still covered by at least one test per browser

title: fix(tests): Reduce ~48s runtime of AI-generated slider bookmarking test
description:
Part of #2308.

`tests/playwright/ai_generated_apps/bookmark/input_slider/test_input_slider_express_bookmarking.py::test_slider_parameters[app-express.py]` takes **~48s on both chromium and webkit** (run [28639206793](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/28639206793)) — it single-handedly dominates its `playwright-ai` shard, where the next-slowest test is ~13s.

Consistent cross-browser slowness points at the test itself: likely many slider drag interactions (each simulated with many small mouse moves) combined with bookmark/reload cycles.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. Identify which steps consume the time (drag simulation vs. reload/bookmark round-trips)
2. Reduce runtime substantially (e.g. fewer slider positions, set values programmatically where dragging isn't the behavior under test) while keeping bookmarking coverage

title: fix(tests): Investigate 56s webkit runtime of test_module_support (0696-resolve-id)
description:
Part of #2308.

`tests/playwright/shiny/bugs/0696-resolve-id/test_0696_resolve_id.py::test_module_support` is the slowest single Playwright test in CI:

- **56.5s on webkit**
- 17.3s on chromium

(Measured in run [28639206793](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/28639206793), Python 3.13.)

The 3× webkit-vs-chromium gap suggests repeated waits, fixed timeouts, or a webkit-specific interaction pattern (e.g. per-event mouse moves) rather than inherent test cost.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. Root cause of the webkit slowdown identified
2. Test runtime reduced substantially (ideally under ~15s on webkit) without losing coverage of module ID resolution

title: epic: Speed up slow Playwright tests in CI
description:
## Summary

Analysis of CI run [28639206793](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/28639206793) (last fully-green `Run tests` on `main`) shows that while most Playwright tests complete in ~1–2 seconds, a handful of tests take 10–55+ seconds each. Durations were collected from the pytest `--durations=6 --durations-min=5.0` reports across all 20 Python 3.13 chromium/webkit playwright jobs (`playwright-shiny`, `playwright-examples`, `playwright-ai` × 4 shards).

These slow tests dominate shard wall-clock time and are the main lever for speeding up CI.

> **Caveat:** pytest only reports the top 6 durations ≥5s per job, so this is a worst-offenders list, not an exhaustive census. Firefox jobs were not sampled but should follow the same pattern.

## Extreme outliers (20s+ per test)

| Test | Duration |
|---|---|
| `tests/playwright/shiny/bugs/0696-resolve-id/test_0696_resolve_id.py::test_module_support` | **56.5s** webkit / 17.3s chromium |

title: feat: Use the app author's navset id for data-tabsetid instead of a random value
description:
## Motivation

Navsets currently mint their `data-tabsetid` (and the derived `tab-<tabsetid>-<index>` pane ids) from a random integer, even when the app author has already supplied a unique `id=` to the navset. Deriving the tabset ID from that user-supplied id would give:

- **Readable, deterministic DOM ids**: `tab-my_tabs-0` instead of `tab-7776790190029-0` — easier debugging, CSS targeting, and browser-devtools work.
- **Stable markup across renders/processes**: friendlier for snapshot tests, HTML diffing, and caching; no order- or seed-dependence.
- **Guaranteed uniqueness for id'd navsets**: Shiny input ids must already be unique within a session (and module namespacing is applied via `resolve_id()`), so the collision question disappears entirely for these navsets.

## Context

#2296 bumped the random ID pool from ~1M to 9T values (13-digit strings, kept below 2**53) after a birthday-paradox collision produced two navsets with the same `data-tabsetid` on one page — causing duplicate DOM ids, broken Bootstrap tab targeting, and CI failures ([example run](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/28619266837/job/84870650451), analysis in #2285). That makes collisions effectively impossible, but the ids remain random and opaque. This issue proposes the complementary improvement: don't be random at all when the author has given us a better id.

Anonymous navsets (no `id=`) and `nav_menu()` dropdowns (which have no user-facing id) would keep the random fallback.

## Prototype

```diff
--- a/shiny/ui/_navs.py
+++ b/shiny/ui/_navs.py
@@ -1617,7 +1617,10 @@ def render_navset(
     selected: Optional[str],
     context: dict[str, Any],
 ) -> tuple[Tag, Tag]:
-    tabsetid = nav_random_int()
+    # Prototype: derive the tabset ID from the user-supplied (already
+    # module-resolved) input id when available; fall back to a random ID for
+    # anonymous navsets.
+    tabsetid = id if id is not None else nav_random_int()
 
     # Separate MetadataNodes from NavSetArgs.
     metadata_args: list[MetadataNode] = []
```

By the time `render_navset()` receives `id`, it is already module-resolved (`NavSet.__init__` calls `resolve_id_or_none()`), so modules produce e.g. `data-tabsetid="mymod-inner_tabs"` / `id="tab-mymod-inner_tabs-0"` with no extra work.

**Validated locally** with the prototype applied:
- Rendering produces the expected markup for plain and module-namespaced navsets.
- All 13 Playwright tests under `tests/playwright/shiny/components/nav/` pass on chromium (kitchensink, navset_bar, page_navbar, nav insert/update paths), confirming shiny.js tab switching, `nav_insert()`'s `getTabIndex()` href parsing, and the Playwright controllers all treat the tabset ID as an opaque string and work with non-numeric values.

## Considerations

- **Snapshot churn**: markup changes for every navset that has an `id`; py-shiny's own `tests/pytest/test_navs.py` expectations and any downstream snapshot tests would need a one-time update.
- **Divergence from R**: R shiny/bslib always use random tabset ids, so rendered markup would no longer be structurally identical across languages (cosmetic only; no shared JS relies on the ID being numeric).
- **Character set**: Shiny ids are restricted enough to be safe in DOM ids and attribute selectors; shiny.js already `$escape`s the value when building selectors.
- `navset_hidden()` and `page_navbar`/`navset_bar` flow through the same `render_navset()` path, so they inherit the behavior automatically.

## Should this live in bslib or py-shiny?

py-shiny. The tabset ID generation for these components is entirely in py-shiny Python code (`shiny/ui/_navs.py` — not vendored from bslib), and the client-side JS needs no changes, so py-shiny can ship it independently. If desired, a parallel parity issue could be filed against rstudio/bslib / rstudio/shiny for the R side, but nothing there blocks this.

Failures are scattered across 2026-05-18 through 2026-07-02 (the most recent run in the analyzed window), so this is an active, ongoing flake rather than a resolved regression.

- https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/26254588938/job/77274069372

title: Epic: Flaky Playwright tests in CI (analysis of last 200 "Run tests" GHA runs)
description:
## Summary

Analyzed the last 200 runs of the `Run tests` GitHub Actions workflow (2026-05-02 → 2026-07-02): 2,579 failed `playwright-*` jobs, 8,635 individual `FAILED tests/...` pytest results across 559 distinct test IDs.

3 runs ([26199691666](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/26199691666), [26236011053](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/26236011053), [26187322801](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/26187322801)) each failed ~500 different tests simultaneously ("Shiny app exited without ever becoming ready" across the whole example suite) — these are CI-environment outages, not test flakiness, and were excluded from the analysis below (they accounted for 87% of raw failure counts).

## 🔴 Genuinely flaky (intermittent, spread across many unrelated commits/weeks)

| Test | Distinct failing runs (of 200) | Pattern | Sub-issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MarkdownStream/basic/test_stream_basic.py::test_validate_stream_basic[webkit]` | 42 | `TimeoutError` waiting on stream render; fails continuously May 3 → Jun 29 | TBD |
| `ai_generated_apps/bookmark/navsets/test_navsets_hidden_bookmarking.py::test_navset_hidden_bookmarking[chromium-navset_hidden-default-NavsetHidden]` | 17 | `AssertionError` on locator attribute; scattered May 18 → Jul 2 (still occurring on most recent run) | TBD |
| `test_examples.py::test_examples[chromium/firefox-examples/airmass/app.py]` | 2 (May 21, Jun 29 — weeks apart) | `AssertionError` | - |
| `test_brand_yml.py::test_brand_yml_kitchensink[firefox/chromium/webkit]` | 2-3 each | `TimeoutError`, scattered May 13/21 | - |
| `test_html_columns.py::test_validate_html_columns[chromium-pandas]` | 2 (May 3, Jun 28 — a month apart) | `Element is not attached to the DOM` (race condition) | - |
| `test_output_info_observers.py::test_output_theme_updates[firefox]` | 2 (May 22, May 28) | `AssertionError` | - |
| `test_inputs_update.py::test_updates[webkit]` | 2 (May 13, May 22) | `TimeoutError` | - |

## 🟡 Time-boxed regressions (already resolved — included for historical record)

These failed together on the same dates, then stopped, indicating a real bug/outage rather than per-test flakiness:

- `test_api_examples.py::test_api_examples[*-shiny/api-examples/poll/app-express.py|app-core.py]` (all 3 browsers) — 15-17 runs each, only May 15–21
- `test_examples.py::test_examples[*-examples/model-score/app.py]` — 17-18 runs, only May 15–21
- `test_external_templates.py::test_external_templates[chromium-py-shiny-templates/monitor-database/app-core.py]` — 15 runs, only May 15–21
- `test_chat_basic.py`/`test_chat_update_user_input.py` (all browsers) — 15 runs each, continuously Jun 16–29, then stopped. Fixed by #2277 (shinychat 0.5.x compat).

## ⚪ Infra-level (not test flakiness, flagging separately)

- The 3 environment-outage runs above.
- Scattered "No space left on device" GHA runner disk-exhaustion failures.

## Methodology

- `gh run list --workflow "Run tests" --limit 200` for run metadata
- `gh api repos/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/runs/<id>/jobs` for job lists, filtered to failed `playwright-*` jobs
- `gh api repos/posit-dev/py-shiny/actions/jobs/<id>/logs` to download raw logs, then grepped `FAILED tests/...` lines from pytest's short summary
- Aggregated by test node ID, cross-referenced against run dates to distinguish genuine intermittent flakiness from clustered/time-boxed regressions

## Sub-issues

Tracking the two most actionable, currently-active flaky tests as sub-issues. The rest of the 🔴 list is lower frequency (2-3 occurrences) — worth a follow-up if they recur, but not yet enough signal to act on individually.

title: docs: Add an example app and/or docs article for test mode
description:
Follow-up to #2269 / PR #2270.

Test mode (the `SHINY_TESTMODE=1` / `App(test_mode=)` flag, `shiny.session.export_test_values()`, the `/dataobj/shinytest` snapshot endpoint + `session.get_test_snapshot_url()`, and the `shiny.playwright.controller.AppTestValues` controller) currently only has API docstrings.

Add user-facing documentation:
- A `shiny/api-examples/` example app demonstrating `export_test_values()` and reading the snapshot with `AppTestValues` in an end-to-end test, and/or
- A short docs article/how-to on testing a Shiny app's reactive state with test mode.

title: fix: Silenced outputs record `None` in the test-mode snapshot
description:
Part of #2269 (noted during PR #2270 review).

When an output raises `SilentException` (e.g. via `req()`), the render pipeline calls `OutBoundMessageQueues.set_value(output_name, None)`, so test mode records `None` for that output. The test-mode snapshot therefore reports `null` for a silenced output rather than either (a) retaining the output's last computed value or (b) omitting it entirely.

Shiny for R keeps the last computed value for an output, so this is a small fidelity gap. Decide the desired behavior and align:
- Retain last value (R-like), or
- Omit silenced outputs from the snapshot, or
- Keep current `null` behavior but document it.

### References
- `shiny/session/_session.py`: the `output_obs` render path (`set_value(output_name, None)` on `SilentException`) and the persistent `test_values` recording.

title: feat: Test-mode snapshot preprocessing (snapshot_preprocess_input/output)
description:
Part of #2269 (deferred from PR #2270).

Shiny for R lets app authors register per-value transforms that run *before* a value is written to the test snapshot, via `snapshotPreprocessInput(inputId, fn)` and `snapshotPreprocessOutput(output, fn)`. These are essential for scrubbing non-deterministic values (timestamps, temp paths, random ids, session tokens) so snapshots diff cleanly across runs.

py-shiny's test mode (PR #2270) does not yet have an equivalent. This issue tracks adding it.

### Scope / open questions
- API shape: session methods and/or free functions (mirroring how `export_test_values` landed in `shiny.session`)? Where do preprocessors live?
- Which blocks: `input` and `output` (as R), and/or `export`?
- How preprocessors are keyed (per input/output id) and applied in `AppSession._handle_test_snapshot` before `_snapshot_safe_value`.
- Namespacing behavior in modules (consistent with the export-name namespacing deviation from R).

### References
- Server handler: `shiny/session/_session.py` `_handle_test_snapshot`
- R behavior: `enableTestSnapshot` in `rstudio/shiny` `R/shiny.R` (`getSnapshotPreprocessInput` / `getSnapshotPreprocessOutput`)

title: `shiny[otel]` should include `opentelemetry-distro` for auto-instrumentation support
description:
### Type

API Reference

### Location

https://shiny.posit.co/py/docs/opentelemetry.html#basic-configuration

### Issue

Other

### Suggested Changes

The standard way to apply opentelemetry instrumentation to a python app is to  run `opentelemetry-instrument app` so in the case of Shiny it would be `opentelemetry-instrument shiny run app.py` (which works perfectly fine)

But the [Shiny documentation](https://shiny.posit.co/py/docs/opentelemetry.html#basic-configuration) describes a manual process that would conflict with auto instrumentation.

`shiny[otel]` only brings the `opentelemetry-sdk` dependency and not `opentelemetry-distro` which is instead needed for the autoinstrumentation to work as it has knowledge of how the instrumentation needs to be configured and initialized for each python library.

If `shiny[otel]` did bring in `opentelemetry-distro[otlp]` that should do (and would also have the benefit of making possible for the user to switch to HTTP or gRPC output easily)

Cross product integration with OTel auto instrumentation.

title: [Bug]: Uncaught TypeError in _shinyResizeObserver.ts when dynamic components/modals are removed
description:
### Component

UI (ui.*)

### Severity

P2 - Medium (workaround exists)

### Shiny Version

1.6.1+

### Python Version

3.12

### Minimal Reproducible Example

```python
from shiny import App, render, ui
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

app_ui = ui.page_fluid(
    ui.input_action_button("open_modal", "Open Modal with Plot"),
)

def server(input, output, session):
    @render.plot
    def my_plot():
        fig, ax = plt.subplots()
        ax.plot([1, 2], [3, 4])
        return fig

    @input.open_modal
    def _():
        ui.modal_show(
            ui.modal(
                ui.card(
                    ui.card_header("Card inside Modal"),
                    ui.output_plot("my_plot"),
                ),
                title="Reproduction Modal",
                easy_close=True
            )
        )

app = App(app_ui, server)
```

### Behavior

When a container that is registered with the `ShinyResizeObserver` (such as a card, sidebar, or a layout component inside a modal) is removed from the DOM, the observer does not automatically stop watching it.

During the cleanup/removal transition:

1. The DOM elements are detached/unbound, which clears their associated jQuery data (`shinyOutputBinding`).
2. The browser triggers a final `ResizeObserver` callback on the resizing/disappearing container.
3. The callback runs query selectors inside the target for `.shiny-bound-output` and finds the detached elements.
4. Because the elements are detached/unbound, calling `$(el).data("shinyOutputBinding")` returns undefined.
5. Destructuring binding and onResize from undefined throws an uncaught JavaScript error, halting the client-side execution.

---

**Proposed Solution**

It seems like the underlying issue is actually in bslib. 

A defensive check or fallback should be added in `_shinyResizeObserver.ts` to safely ignore elements whose bindings have already been torn down or are not yet set:

```typescript
const outputData = $(el).data("shinyOutputBinding");
if (!outputData) return;
const { binding, onResize } = outputData;
if (!binding || !binding.resize) return;
```

Or using a fallback:

```typescript
const { binding, onResize } = $(el).data("shinyOutputBinding") || {};
if (!binding || !binding.resize) return;
```

**Disclaimer**: This Bug Report was prepared with the help of Antigravity and manually verified.
I greatly appreciate all the hard work the maintainers have poured into the shiny ecosystem and would not like to add AI slop here 😅 

### Error Messages (if any)

```shell
Uncaught TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'binding' of '$(...).data(...)' as it is undefined.
    at _shinyResizeObserver.ts:81:21
    at NodeList.forEach (<anonymous>)
    at ResizeObserver.<anonymous> (_shinyResizeObserver.ts:78:12)
```

### Environment

```markdown
Python package: shiny (version 1.6.0 / 1.6.1+)
Underlying UI package: bslib (frontend assets compiled from rstudio/bslib version 0.10.0 / 0.11.0+)

OS: Win10
Browser: Edge 149.0.4022.69
```

"""

problem_str = """
input_checkbox_group accepts selected keys as ints, but update_checkbox_group does not.
The intention is to have all the options checked by default. There is no problem when 
initiating the checkbox group, but there is a problem when it updates.
\n Bonus idea:\n
It would be great if you could just pass a bool as an argument to check all boxes passed.
"""

checkbox_init = {
    "label": "Select multiple options:",
    "choices": DICT["Foo"],
    "selected": [k for k in DICT["Foo"].keys()],
}

app_ui = ui.page_fluid(
    ui.h2(problem_h2),
    ui.p(problem_str),
    ui.input_radio_buttons(
        "select_key", "Select a dictionary:", list(DICT.keys()), selected="Foo"
    ),
    ui.card(
        ui.card_header("Bugged checkbox_group"),
        ui.p(
            "After selecting a dict above, the options will be unchecked. They should be checked."
        ),
        ui.input_checkbox_group("check_group_bad", **checkbox_init),
    ),
    ui.card(
        ui.card_header("This checkbox_group works properly"),
        ui.p("But it required an extra step of converting keys to strings"),
        ui.input_checkbox_group("check_group_good", **checkbox_init),
    ),
)


def server(input, output, session):
    @reactive.effect
    @reactive.event(input.select_key, ignore_init=True)
    def _():
        choices = DICT[input.select_key()]
        ui.update_checkbox_group(
            "check_group_bad", choices=choices, selected=[k for k in choices.keys()]
        )
        ui.update_checkbox_group(
            "check_group_good",
            choices=choices,
            selected=[str(k) for k in choices.keys()],
        )


app = App(app_ui, server)
```

### Behavior

Current: `update_checkbox_group()` with `selected=some_dict` where the type of some_dict is dict[int, str], does not check the boxes. This is unexpected, because `input_checkbox_group()` accepts dictionaries with int keys and quietly converts them to strings. 
Expected: `update_checkbox_group()` should quietly convert dictionary integers to string the same way `input_checkbox_group()` does for the `selected` parameter. 
Current workaound: converting int keys from dict to string works just fine. e.g `selected=[str(k) for k in choices_dict.keys()]`

### Error Messages (if any)

```shell
No errors, shiny silently doesn't check any boxes when none of the `selected=` hit.
```

### Environment

```markdown
OS: Windows 11
Browser: Chrome
Dependencies: None
```

title: feat: Add test mode with export_test_values() and /dataobj/shinytest snapshot endpoint
description:
## Summary

Port R Shiny's **test mode** to py-shiny: a read-only per-session JSON snapshot endpoint exposing `{input, output, export}`, plus an `export_test_values()` API so app authors can surface internal reactive values. This is the server-side foundation for a future shinytest2-like snapshot-testing story in Python.

This is **Phase A** (server-side snapshot endpoint + API). First-class Playwright/automation access to these values is a later **Phase B** and is out of scope here.

## Motivation

R Shiny's test mode powers `shinytest2` snapshot testing: it registers a per-session `/dataobj/shinytest` JSON endpoint returning `{input, output, export}`, and `exportTestValues()` lets app authors expose internal reactive values for snapshotting. py-shiny has the building blocks (input serialization, cached output values, a per-session request router) but nothing is wired up, and there is no `export_test_values()` equivalent.

## Scope (Phase A)

### Enabling
- Enable via environment variable **`SHINY_TESTMODE=1`** only (mirrors the existing `SHINY_DEV_MODE` pattern in `html_dependencies.py`).
- A constructor argument (`App(..., test_mode=...)`) is deferred to a later phase.
- When off: zero behavioral change — no value recording, the endpoint 404s, `export_test_values()` is a cheap no-op.

### `export_test_values()` API
- Module-level function **and** session method (`session.export_test_values(**kwargs)`).
- Called as `export_test_values(my_val=lambda: total() + 1, count=my_calc)` — each value is a zero-arg callable / `reactive.calc`, evaluated lazily inside a reactive context at snapshot time.
- Module-level form resolves the current session via `get_current_session()`.
- Export names are **namespaced** with the module's `ns` prefix (consistent with inputs/outputs; note R does not namespace).
- Last-registration-wins on duplicate names.

### Snapshot endpoint
- Auto-registered at **`/session/<token>/dataobj/shinytest`** (R-compatible path) when test mode is on.
- Returns `{ "input": {...}, "output": {...}, "export": {...} }` (R's singular keys, kept as-is).
- Handler wraps work in `session_context(self)` + `isolate()` (same pattern as `dynamic_route`).
- **`input`** — serialized current inputs (dedicated snapshot serialization path, not the bookmark `_serialize`, so it doesn't write files to a `state_dir` or silently drop unserializables).
- **`output`** — **last-known-value record**: maintain a per-session dict of the most recent value computed for each output (recorded where output values are set). Outputs that never computed are absent. (Matches R semantics.)
- **`export`** — each registered callable evaluated lazily at request time.

### Serialization fidelity
- Best-effort coercion; values that can't be JSON-encoded are wrapped in a visible tagged marker (e.g. `{"__shiny_serialization_error__": "<message>"}`) rather than silently stringified or hard-failing.
- Sort keys for deterministic, cleanly-diffable snapshots.

### URL helper
- Add `session.get_test_snapshot_url()` (R parity with `session$getTestSnapshotUrl()`), including a cache-busting `nonce`. Included in Phase A.

## Out of scope (deferred to Phase B)
- Registering the built-but-unused `shiny/www/shared/shiny-testmode.js` eval-driving helper (for driving an app from a parent frame).
- First-class Playwright controller / `page` helper access to snapshot values.
- `App(test_mode=...)` constructor argument.

## Related
- #1156 (Add testing API for py-shiny — broader testing-namespace request)
- #1281 (Epic — Testing shiny apps; Playwright controller work)
- #1980 (Save and restore state — touches the same input `_serialize` path)

title: Recalculating overlay gets stuck on outputs inside hidden navset tabs (regression in 1.6.1)
[Feature]: Pass additional parameters from `navset_card_*()` to `card()`
description:
### Category

UI Components

### Scope

Quality of Life

### Problem

I came across a situation where I wanted a `navset_card_pill` inside an outer card. The navset card held several elements under each tab, meaning the inner card needed a scrollbar to view all elements. My preference in this scenario would have been to have the outer card scroll and the inner card expand to its full height. The trouble is that you can't pass additional parameters to `navset_card_pill` such as `style`, `height`, or `fill`.

My workaround was to wrap the `navset_card_pill` in a `div` to set `height="auto"`. This was fine. It has a minor inconvenience of extra margin below the inner card, but that isn't very difficult to correct with some CSS.

## Reproducible Example

Observe the scrolling behavior of the left column when the window height is small (for example on a mobile device in landscape mode). The navset card is becomes very short and is forced to scroll.

 ```python
from shiny import App, ui

import lorem

app_ui = ui.page_navbar(
    ui.nav_panel(
        "Main",
        ui.layout_columns(
            ui.card(
                ui.card_header("Outer Card"),
                ui.p("Some UI element above"),
                ui.navset_card_pill(
                    ui.nav_panel("Tab 1", ui.p(lorem.get_paragraph(3))),
                    # can't pass additional arguments through to card()
                ),
                ui.p("Some UI element below"),
            ),
            ui.card("Right column", ui.p(lorem.get_paragraph(3))),
            col_widths=[6, 6],
        ),
    ),
    title="App",
    fillable=True,
)


def server(input, output, session):
    pass


app = App(app_ui, server)

```

An example of the workaround:

<details>

```python
from shiny import App, ui

import lorem

app_ui = ui.page_navbar(
    ui.nav_panel(
        "Main",
        ui.layout_columns(
            ui.card(
                ui.card_header("Outer Card"),
                ui.p("Some UI element above"),
                ui.div(
                    ui.navset_card_pill(
                        ui.nav_panel("Tab 1", ui.p(lorem.get_paragraph(3))),
                    ),
                    height="auto",
                ),
                ui.p("Some UI element below"),
            ),
            ui.card("Right column", ui.p(lorem.get_paragraph(3))),
            col_widths=[6, 6],
        ),
    ),
    title="App",
    fillable=True,
)


def server(input, output, session):
    pass


app = App(app_ui, server)

```

</details>

Shiny: 1.6.2
Python: 3.14.5
OS: Windows 11
Browser: tested in Firefox and Chrome


### Solution

Similar to #1451, passing through other parameters to `card()` would be useful. That would offer more freedom for users to style the `navset_card_*` cards. Perhaps `kwargs` would be suitable here?

title: Bug: `AttributeError: 'TagifiedTag' object has no attribute 'insert'`
description:
Ex error output:
```
2026/05/21 4:42:49 PM:   File "/app/python/env/lib/python3.13/site-packages/shiny/_app.py", line 486, in _render_page
2026/05/21 4:42:49 PM:     ui_res.insert(
2026/05/21 4:42:49 PM:     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^
2026/05/21 4:42:49 PM: AttributeError: 'TagifiedTag' object has no attribute 'insert'
```

From: https://github.com/posit-dev/py-htmltools/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#070---2026-05-21

> ### Breaking changes
> 
> * `Tagifiable.tagify()`'s return annotation is now `Tagified`, a new type alias for the union of fully-tagified shapes (`TagifiedNode | float | None | Sequence[Tagified]`, mirroring `TagChild`). Custom `.tagify()` implementations annotated with bare `TagList` / `Tag` return types should switch to `-> Tagified`, or drop the annotation. Runtime behavior of correct implementations is unchanged. (posit-dev/py-htmltools#105, posit-dev/py-htmltools#116)
> 
> * The result of `.tagify()` is now **immutable**. Calling `.append`, `.extend`, `.insert`, `.add_class`, `__setitem__`, or the context-manager `with` form on a tagified value raises `AttributeError` and is a static type error. Mutate on the buildable `Tag` / `TagList` side, then call `.tagify()` once to produce the render-ready result. (posit-dev/py-htmltools#116)
> 
> * `TagList.tagify()` now raises `TypeError` at the boundary when a child's `.tagify()` returns un-tagified content (e.g. a bare `TagList` containing a still-`Tagifiable` object). The error names the offending class and slot index so buggy `.tagify()` implementations surface at the source. The render-time `RuntimeError` for the same family of violations has been clarified. (posit-dev/py-htmltools#7, posit-dev/py-htmltools#105, posit-dev/py-htmltools#112, posit-dev/py-htmltools#116)
> 

---------------------------------

## Fix

* Please require the latest shiny release: `shiny >= 1.6.2`
* Or restrict your htmltools version: `htmltools < 0.7.0`

Fixed in #2244

title: Remove temporary htmltools git URL workaround in Makefile once htmltools 0.7.0 ships
description:
## Context

PR #2244 (https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shiny/pull/2244) adds support for the new `Tagified` type alias from py-htmltools 0.7.0. Until htmltools 0.7.0 is on PyPI, py-shiny's `pyproject.toml` pins `htmltools` to a git branch:

```toml
"htmltools @ git+https://github.com/posit-dev/py-htmltools.git@schloerke/tagify-tag-class-issue"
```

uv refuses to resolve `py-shiny-templates/requirements.txt` while a transitive URL-pinned dep isn't repeated as a direct requirement. To unblock `playwright-examples` CI, the `ci-install-py-shiny-templates-deps` target now pre-installs htmltools from the branch:

```makefile
ci-install-py-shiny-templates-deps: FORCE
    uv pip install \
        "htmltools @ git+https://github.com/posit-dev/py-htmltools.git@schloerke/tagify-tag-class-issue" \
        -r py-shiny-templates/requirements.txt
```

## Action

Once htmltools 0.7.0 is released on PyPI **and** PR #2244's `pyproject.toml` has been flipped to `htmltools>=0.7.0`, revert the Makefile target to:

```makefile
ci-install-py-shiny-templates-deps: FORCE
    uv pip install -r py-shiny-templates/requirements.txt
```

Both changes (`pyproject.toml` flip + Makefile revert) are marked with `TODO(htmltools-105)` in the codebase.

Refs: posit-dev/py-htmltools#105, posit-dev/py-htmltools#106

title: js-react template: output renderComp throws on null initial payload
description:
## Summary

The `js-react` `shiny create` template's example app raises a client-side error on first render:

```
Cannot destructure property 'value' of 'object null' as it is null
```

The error is thrown inside the template's own `renderComp` in `shiny/templates/package/js-react/srcts/index.tsx`:

```tsx
makeReactOutput<{ value: string }>({
  name: "custom-component-output",
  selector: "custom-component-output",
  renderComp: ({ value }) => (   // ← destructures `value`, but the payload is `null`
    <div style={{ backgroundColor: value, ... }} />
  ),
});
```

When `@posit-dev/shiny-bindings-react`'s `renderValue(el, payload)` is invoked with `payload === null` during the initial output lifecycle, the destructure of `null` throws.

## Reproduction

```bash
shiny create --template js-react --package-name my_component --dir /tmp/my_component
cd /tmp/my_component
npm ci && npm run build
pip install -e . shiny
shiny run example-app/app.py
# open in browser → red error overlay / DevTools console shows the destructure error
```

## Fix (probably template-side)

Either guard the renderComp:

```tsx
renderComp: (data) => {
  if (!data) return null;
  return <div style={{ backgroundColor: data.value, ... }} />;
}
```

…or change `@posit-dev/shiny-bindings-react` to skip rendering when the payload is null.

## Pre-existing, not a regression

Verified the bug is unrelated to #2237's lodash bump — it reproduces against both the original `lodash` `4.17.21` lockfile from `main` and the patched `4.18.1` lockfile in #2237. See #2237 for the testing setup that surfaced this.

title: Value._set() identity check causes server-side dedup for event-priority inputs
description:
## Summary

When `Shiny.setInputValue(name, value, {priority: 'event'})` is called from JavaScript, the `priority: "event"` option correctly bypasses the client-side deduplication layer (`InputNoResendDecorator`). However, the Python server-side `Value._set()` method has an identity check (`self._value is value`) that silently drops the update when CPython interns the value — most notably for small integers and short strings.

This means repeatedly sending the same integer value (e.g., `42`) with `priority: "event"` only fires the reactive effect once, even though R Shiny would fire it every time. This is inconsistent with R Shiny's `dedupe = FALSE` behavior.

## Root cause

In `shiny/reactive/_reactives.py`, `Value._set()` (line ~491):

```python
def _set(self, value: T) -> bool:
    if self._value is value:
        return False
    ...
```

CPython interns small integers (-5 to 256) and some short strings, so `42 is 42` is `True`. Each JSON deserialization of `42` returns the same interned Python object, causing the `is` check to pass and skip reactive invalidation.

For non-interned values like lists (`[1, 2, 3]`), each JSON parse creates a new object, so `is` returns `False` and the reactive effect fires correctly.

## Reproduction

```javascript
// This only fires the server-side reactive effect ONCE, no matter how many clicks:
document.getElementById('btn').addEventListener('click', function() {
    Shiny.setInputValue('my_input', 42, {priority: 'event'});
});
```

```python
@reactive.effect
@reactive.event(input.my_input)
def _count():
    # Only called once, even after multiple button clicks
    counter.set(counter() + 1)
```

## Expected behavior

With `priority: "event"`, every call to `Shiny.setInputValue()` should trigger the reactive effect on the server, regardless of whether the value is the same — matching R Shiny's behavior.

## Possible fix

The `is` identity check in `Value._set()` was likely intended as a performance optimization. Options:

1. **Remove the `is` check entirely** — always invalidate when `_set()` is called. This matches how `_manage_inputs` unconditionally calls `_set()` for every incoming message.
2. **Add a force/dedupe parameter** — allow callers to bypass the identity check, similar to R Shiny's `dedupe` parameter. The session's `_manage_inputs` could pass this through based on input message metadata.
3. **Use equality (`==`) instead of identity (`is`)** — this would fix the interning issue but would still deduplicate genuinely equal values, which may not be desired for event-priority inputs.

## R Shiny reference

- R Shiny's `setInputValue` with `priority: "event"` bypasses both client-side and server-side dedup: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/75a63716e578976965daeadde81af7166a50faac/R/shiny.R#L728
- The `dedupe` field controls whether the server compares the new value to the old value before invalidating

Two docstrings use a bare `:` as the Returns label in NumPy-style format, which renders as an orphaned colon in the generated API docs:

> `:  A toast header object.`

**`/api/core/render.image.html`** (and express equivalent)
The Returns section shows:

This was caught by an automated site audit of the PR preview.

Both docstrings use the pattern:

```python
Returns
-------
:
    Description here.
```

The bare `:` is intended as an anonymous return label, but it renders literally in the docs output.

Replace the bare `:` with an explicit type label in each docstring:

**`shiny/ui/_toast.py` — `toast_header`:**

Returns
-------
ToastHeader
    A toast header object.

title: bug: Dangling reactivity - reactive objects persist after dynamic UI is removed
description:
## Summary

_Hat tip to @khusmann for clearly articulating this problem._

When dynamic UI is removed (via `remove_ui()`, `@render.ui` re-rendering, or toggling visibility), the server-side reactive objects associated with that UI are not cleaned up. This creates three types of dangling state:

1. **Dangling effects** -- `reactive.effect` objects created for dynamic UI keep firing even after the UI is removed from the DOM.
2. **Dangling calcs** -- `reactive.calc` objects persist in memory with stale values. `Calc_` has no `destroy()` method at all.
3. **Dangling input values** -- `input.foo()` still returns the last value for inputs that no longer exist in the DOM.

1. Click **Create Panel** to add 2-3 panels. Each creates a module with an auto-incrementing `reactive.effect`, a `reactive.calc`, and a dynamic `input_text`.
2. Uncheck **Show dynamic UI** on a panel -- the sidebar monitor shows the effect count still incrementing and the input value still present.
3. Click **Remove this panel** -- the entry turns red and shows `[REMOVED]`, but the effect count keeps going up and the input/calc values persist.

## Root Cause

The server has no concept of reactive object ownership or scoping tied to UI lifecycle:

- `insert_ui()` / `remove_ui()` are purely client-side DOM operations. The server sends a message and forgets about it.
- Module servers create reactive objects that register with the session, but nothing tracks which module "owns" which reactive objects.
- There is no "reactive scope" that groups reactive objects and can destroy them as a unit.
- `Calc_` lacks basic lifecycle management -- no `destroy()`, no `session.on_ended()` callback.

### What IS cleaned up today

| Mechanism | How |
|-----------|-----|
| Output effects when re-registered with same ID | `Outputs.remove()` calls `effect.destroy()` |
| All `Effect_` on session end | Each registers `session.on_ended(self.destroy)` |
| Client-side input/output bindings | `shinyUnbindAll(el)` before DOM replacement |
| Output suspension when hidden | `_manage_hidden()` suspends (but does NOT destroy) |

### What is NOT cleaned up

| Mechanism |
|-----------|
| `reactive.effect` from module server after `remove_ui` |
| `reactive.calc` (no `destroy()` method exists) |
| Server-side `input.*` values for removed DOM inputs |
| Any server-side state tracking for `insert_ui` / `remove_ui` |

## Prior Art

### py-shiny

- #399 -- `remove_ui` input values persist. Closed as expected behavior with manual workaround.
- The todo list example (`shiny/api-examples/todo_list/app-core.py:93-97`) manually calls `effect.destroy()` and comments that this is needed because `remove_ui` only removes HTML.

### R Shiny (rstudio/shiny)

This is a long-standing problem in R Shiny as well:

- [rstudio/shiny#2281](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/2281) -- The canonical issue: `insertUI`/`callModule` to add, `removeUI`/??? to remove. No mechanism to deactivate a module server instance.
- [rstudio/shiny#825](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/825) -- "Reactive subDomains" proposal (2016). Proposes `createSubDomain()` where ending the subdomain destroys all reactive objects created within it.
- [rstudio/shiny#2374](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/2374) -- Request to delete server-side input values on `removeUI()`.
- [rstudio/shiny#3812](https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/3812) -- Add hooks around dynamic UI lifecycle.

### Current Workaround

Users must manually track every `reactive.effect` and call `.destroy()` on removal. This doesn't scale, doesn't work for `reactive.calc` (no destroy method), and doesn't clean up input values.

## Possible Directions (not prescriptive)

- Add `destroy()` to `Calc_`
- Reactive scoping / ownership tracking (a la rstudio/shiny#825 subDomains)
- Server-side awareness of which inputs/outputs belong to which dynamic UI context
- Coordination between `remove_ui` / `@render.ui` and server-side cleanup
- Module-level teardown mechanism

title: feat: Expose missing App attributes in Express via app_opts() and/or an app accessor
description:
## Problem

Shiny Express apps configure app-level options via `app_opts()`, but it only covers a subset of what can be set on a `shiny.App` object in Core mode. Several important `App` attributes are **completely inaccessible** from Express:

| Attribute | Core mode | Express `app_opts()` |
|-----------|-----------|----------------------|
| `static_assets` | `App(...)` constructor | ✅ supported |
| `bookmark_store` | `App(...)` constructor | ✅ supported |
| `debug` | `App(...)` constructor | ✅ supported |
| `sanitize_errors` | `app.sanitize_errors = True` | ❌ missing |
| `sanitize_error_msg` | `app.sanitize_error_msg = "..."` | ❌ missing |
| `sanitize_otel_errors` | `app.sanitize_otel_errors = False` | ❌ missing |
| `lib_prefix` | `app.lib_prefix = "assets/"` | ❌ missing |

In Core mode, an app sets these like:

```python
app = App(app_ui, server)
app.sanitize_errors = True
app.sanitize_otel_errors = False
app.sanitize_error_msg = "Something went wrong."
```

In Express, there is no equivalent — `app_opts()` doesn't support any of them and the underlying `App` object is never exposed to the user.

## Proposed Solutions

### Option A: Extend `app_opts()` with all missing attributes

Add the missing parameters to the existing `app_opts()` function:

```python
app_opts(
    sanitize_errors=True,
    sanitize_otel_errors=False,
    sanitize_error_msg="Something went wrong.",
    lib_prefix="assets/",
)
```

**Pros:** Consistent with the existing pattern; all options in one place.  
**Cons:** `app_opts()` grows with every new `App` attribute; may lag behind future additions.

### Option B: Provide an accessor to the underlying `App` object

Expose a function (e.g., `express.get_app()`) that returns the live `App` instance, allowing direct attribute mutation:

```python
from shiny.express import get_app

get_app().sanitize_errors = True
get_app().sanitize_otel_errors = False
```

**Pros:** No need to update `app_opts()` every time `App` gains a new attribute; users have full control; mirrors the Core mode experience.  
**Cons:** Requires the `App` to exist at call time (it's created during `create_express_app()`); needs careful handling of the execution lifecycle; slightly less discoverable.

### Option C: Both — extend `app_opts()` and add an accessor

Keep `app_opts()` for the most common options, and add `get_app()` as an escape hatch for advanced use.

## Recommendation

Implement **Option C**:
1. Add `sanitize_errors`, `sanitize_otel_errors`, and `sanitize_error_msg` to `app_opts()` since they're immediately needed and commonly configured.
2. Add a `get_app()` (or similar name — `current_app()`, `express_app()`?) accessor as an escape hatch so future `App` attributes don't require `app_opts()` updates.

The naming of the accessor is worth discussion — options include:
- `express.get_app()`
- `express.current_app()`
- `express.app()` (but could conflict with the `app` module)

## Related

- `shiny/express/_run.py` — `app_opts()` and `AppOpts` TypedDict
- `shiny/_app.py` — `App` class with all mutable attributes
- `examples/req/app.py` — Core mode example using `app.sanitize_errors = True`

title: Feature Request: Server-side File Selection (Similar to R Shiny's shinyFiles)
description:
# Description
I'm working with Python Shiny and need to implement server-side file selection functionality (let users select files that already exist on the server, not upload local files from the client side).
In R Shiny, the shinyFiles package provides a mature solution for this scenario: it can list files/directories on the server, allow users to navigate server directories interactively, select files/folders, and return the server-side paths to the app logic.
I wonder if Python Shiny currently has an official/community-maintained package/tool that achieves the same goal? If not, I'd like to discuss the feasible approaches to develop such a feature for Python Shiny.
# Current Workaround (Temporary Solution)
At present, I've implemented a basic version by:
Reading the server directory via os.listdir()/pathlib in the server logic
Dynamically generating a dropdown/checkbox group with ui.input_select()/ui.input_checkbox_group() to display file lists
Returning the full server path of the selected file to read/process it
However, this approach has limitations:
No interactive directory navigation (users can't browse subdirectories on the server)
Lack of file type filtering, pagination (for large file lists), and other user-friendly features
No support for selecting directories (only files)
# Questions & Discussion Points
Does Python Shiny have a built-in/third-party solution equivalent to R's shinyFiles?
If not, what's the recommended architecture to develop this feature? For example:
Extending Python Shiny's UI components to support interactive directory browsing
Wrapping file system operations into reactive functions to sync server directory changes
Ensuring security (restricting access to specific server directories to avoid path traversal risks)
Are there any existing design patterns/APIs in Python Shiny that we can reuse for this development?
 
Thanks for your attention and guidance!

title: Automatic Naming for reactive.value() Objects
description:
## Problem

When using OpenTelemetry logging, reactive values currently require either explicit naming or fall back to `<unnamed>` in log messages. This makes it difficult to identify which values are being updated in logs, reducing the observability benefits of the telemetry system.

```python
# Current behavior without automatic naming
counter = reactive.value(0)
counter.set(42)
# Logs: "Set reactiveVal <unnamed>"  # Not helpful!

# Current workaround - manual naming required
counter = reactive.value(0, name="counter")
counter.set(42)
# Logs: "Set reactiveVal counter"  # Better, but manual
```

For input values specifically, there's no way to distinguish them from user-created reactive values in logs, even though they represent fundamentally different concepts in a Shiny application.

## Proposed Solution

Implement automatic name inference for `reactive.value()` objects using stack inspection, with special handling for input values to add an `input.` prefix (except for `.clientdata` keys).

### Automatic Name Inference

When a `reactive.value()` is created without an explicit `name` parameter, inspect the call stack to parse the assignment statement and extract the variable name:

```python
# Automatically infers name as "counter"
counter = reactive.value(0)
counter.set(42)
# Logs: "Set reactiveVal counter"

# Works with attribute assignment too
class MyApp:
    def __init__(self):
        self.counter = reactive.value(0)  # Infers name as "counter"
```

### Input Value Prefix

Input values managed by the `Inputs` class should automatically receive an `input.` prefix to distinguish them from user-created reactive values:

```python
# In Shiny application
def server(input, output, session):
    # Input values automatically get "input." prefix
    value = input.slider()
    # Internal logs: "Set reactiveVal input.slider"

    # User-created values have no prefix
    counter = reactive.value(0)
    counter.set(42)
    # Logs: "Set reactiveVal counter"
```

Exception: Keys starting with `.` (like `.clientdata_output_plot_hidden`) should not receive the `input.` prefix and should use the full key as the name.

## Benefits

1. **Better Observability**: Log messages automatically include meaningful names without manual effort
2. **Clear Distinction**: `input.` prefix makes it easy to distinguish input values from user-created reactive values
3. **Backward Compatible**: Explicit `name` parameter still works and takes priority
4. **Zero Configuration**: Works out of the box for most common patterns

## Implementation Details

The implementation uses Python's `inspect.stack()` to walk up call frames and parse source code with regex patterns:

```python
def _try_infer_name(self) -> str | None:
    import inspect
    import re

    for frame_info in inspect.stack()[2:]:
        # Skip internal shiny package code
        # Get source line and match patterns like:
        # - var_name = reactive.value(...)
        # - self.var_name = reactive.value(...)
        ...
```

For input values, the `Inputs` class sets names in both `__setitem__` and `__getitem__`:

```python
def __setitem__(self, key: str, value: Value[Any]) -> None:
    if not key.startswith("."):
        value._name = f"input.{key}"
    self._map[self._ns(key)] = value

def __getitem__(self, key: str) -> Value[Any]:
    if key not in self._map:
        value_name = (
            original_key if original_key.startswith(".")
            else f"input.{original_key}"
        )
        new_value = Value[Any](read_only=True, name=value_name)
        self._map[key] = new_value
    return self._map[key]
```

## Edge Cases

The automatic inference may fail (returning `None`) in these cases:

- List comprehensions: `values = [reactive.value(i) for i in range(3)]`
- No assignment: `reactive.value(0)` used inline
- Complex expressions where parsing is ambiguous

In these cases, the name remains `None` and logs show `<unnamed>`, which is acceptable since these are typically not meaningful reactive values for logging purposes.

## Testing

Comprehensive test coverage includes:

- Explicit name parameter
- Inferred names from simple assignments
- Inferred names from attribute assignments
- Explicit name overrides inference
- Unnamed values when inference fails
- Names used in log messages
- `Inputs` class prefix behavior
- `.clientdata` prefix skipping
- Name overriding after creation

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Manual naming only**: Rejected because it places too much burden on users and reduces observability
2. **Global registry**: Rejected due to complexity and potential memory leaks
3. **Decorator-based naming**: Rejected because `reactive.value()` is typically created in `__init__` or function scope where decorators don't apply naturally

## Questions

- Should we support more complex assignment patterns (e.g., tuple unpacking)?
  - A: No
- Should there be a way to disable automatic inference globally?
  - A: No
- Should output values also get a prefix (e.g., `output.plot`)?
  - A: No. They will be logged with `output <NAME>`

   - `patch_tracing_state(*, tracing_enabled)` - Context manager for temporary patching
   - Both use keyword-only arguments, not exported in public API
   - Replaced 22+ occurrences across 4 test files
- ✅ **Modifier tracking via function attributes** instead of ContextVar:
   - Decorators set `_shiny_otel_label_modifier` attribute on functions
   - Attribute automatically passes through `@functools.wraps()`
   - Cleaner, simpler approach (~270 lines removed)

## Acceptance Criteria

- ✅ Reactive computations create spans when `SHINY_OTEL_COLLECT >= reactivity`
- ✅ Spans have descriptive labels (function names, not just "reactive")
- ✅ Source location attributes (`code.filepath`, `code.lineno`) included when available
- ✅ Module namespaces reflected in span names
- ✅ Async context propagates correctly (child spans nest under reactive.update)
- ✅ Spans include parent reactive.update span context
- ✅ **Bonus**: Code duplication eliminated through lazy evaluation (~150 lines reduced)
- ✅ **Bonus**: Strong typing with no suppressions (except known OTel SDK limitation)
- ✅ **Bonus**: Test code improved with helper utilities for better encapsulation
- ✅ **Bonus**: Modifier system simplified with function attributes (~270 lines removed)

## Implementation Improvements

1. **Callable Name Parameter** - Added support for `name: str | Callable[[], str]` in span wrappers
   - Enables lazy evaluation of expensive name generation
   - Only called if collection is enabled
   - Eliminates if/else duplication

2. **Top-Level Imports** - Moved OTel imports to module level
   - Removes repeated inline import overhead during execution
   - Cleaner code structure in both production and test code

3. **Separate Try/Catch** - `extract_source_ref()` uses separate blocks
   - Maximizes attribute extraction even if some operations fail
   - More robust error handling

4. **Test Helper Utilities** - Internal functions for test isolation
   - `reset_tracing_state(*, tracing_enabled=None)` - Replaces direct state manipulation
   - `patch_tracing_state(*, tracing_enabled)` - Replaces `unittest.mock.patch`
   - Better encapsulation, cleaner test code, easier refactoring

5. **Modifier Tracking via Function Attributes** (replaces ContextVar approach)
   - **Removed**: ~100 lines of ContextVar implementation (`reactive_modifier_context()`, etc.)
   - **Removed**: ~170 lines of tests (`TestReactiveModifierContext`)
   - **Added**: Helper functions `get_otel_label_modifier()` and `set_otel_label_modifier()`
   - **Rationale**: Leverages `@functools.wraps()` automatic attribute passing, simpler design
   - **Impact**: Modifiers "baked in" at decoration time, not runtime

6. **Eager Label Generation** (replaces lazy approach)
   - **Removed**: `_get_otel_label()` helper methods from `Calc_` and `Effect_`
   - **Change**: Generate label once during `__init__`, pass string to span wrapper
   - **Rationale**: With modifier available at init time, no need for lazy evaluation
   - **Impact**: Simpler code, fewer method calls

7. **Modifier Helper Functions** - Centralized API in `_labels.py`
   - `get_otel_label_modifier(func)` - Retrieve modifier string from function
   - `set_otel_label_modifier(func, modifier, *, mode)` - Set/combine modifiers
   - Three modes: `"prepend"` (default), `"append"`, `"replace"`
   - **Rationale**: Clean API for future decorators (`@reactive.cache`, `@reactive.debounce`)
   - **Impact**: Extensible design, well-documented for future enhancements

8. **Code Reduction** - ~420 lines eliminated total:
   - Calc: 67% reduction (40 → 12 lines)
   - Effect: 50% reduction (90 → 45 lines)
   - Output: 48% reduction (25 → 13 lines)
   - Modifier system: ~270 lines removed (ContextVar + tests)

## Files Created

- ✅ `shiny/otel/_labels.py`
- ✅ `tests/pytest/test_otel_reactive_execution.py` (15 tests, all passing)

- ✅ `tests/pytest/test_otel_session.py` (updated to use test helpers)
- ✅ `tests/pytest/test_otel_reactive_flush.py` (updated to use test helpers)

## Test Results

- ✅ Black: Formatted
- ✅ isort: Sorted

title: epic: OpenTelemetry Integration for py-shiny
description:
## Overview

Implement comprehensive OpenTelemetry (OTel) tracing and logging for py-shiny, providing observability into Shiny application behavior with minimal performance overhead. This implementation follows the R Shiny approach but adapts it to Python idioms (async/await, context managers, decorators, contextvars).

## Goals

- **5-level collection granularity**: `none`, `session`, `reactive_update`, `reactivity`, `all`
- **Async-aware span propagation** using Python's `contextvars`
- **Lazy initialization** with minimal performance impact (< 50μs per span)
- **Dual configuration**: Environment variables (`SHINY_OTEL_COLLECT`) and programmatic API (`otel_collect` context manager)
- **Source location attribution** for reactive computations
- **Error sanitization** and proper exception recording
- **Standard OTel compatibility** with backends like Jaeger, Zipkin, etc.

## Architecture

New public module `shiny/otel/` containing:
- Core tracer/logger initialization
- Collection level management
- Context propagation utilities
- Span creation helpers
- Attribute extraction (source refs, HTTP metadata)
- Error handling and sanitization
- User-facing decorators and context managers

## Dependencies

**Phase 1:** Add `opentelemetry-api>=1.20.0` as required dependency
**Phase 10:** Evaluate optional dependency group approach (`pip install shiny[telemetry]`)

## Success Criteria

- [x] OTel integration works with all 5 collection levels
- [x] Session lifecycle spans include correct attributes (session ID, HTTP metadata)
- [x] Reactive execution spans nest correctly under reactive update spans
- [x] Async context propagation maintains correct parent-child relationships
- [x] Users can control collection via environment variable and context managers (environment variable ✅, context manager pending Phase 7)
- [x] Performance overhead < 50μs per span
- [x] Test coverage > 90% for OTel code
- [x] Complete documentation and example applications
- [x] Compatible with standard OTel backends

---

## Sub-Issues

This epic is broken down into 10 phases, each corresponding to a sub-issue:

### 1. ✅ Foundation (Core OTel Infrastructure) [#2132]
Set up basic OTel infrastructure with tracer/logger initialization and collection level management.
**Status**: Merged in PR #2143

### 2. ✅ Session Lifecycle Instrumentation [#2133]
Add OTel spans for session start/end and HTTP/WebSocket connections.
**Status**: Merged in PR #2146

### 3. ✅ Reactive Flush Instrumentation [#2134]
Add "reactive update" spans that wrap each flush cycle, serving as parent for all reactive spans.
**Status**: Merged in PR #2148

### 4. ✅ Reactive Execution Instrumentation [#2135]
Instrument individual reactive computations (calcs, effects, outputs) with descriptive labels and source attribution.
**Status**: Merged in PR #2149

### 5. ✅ Value Updates and Logging [#2136]
Log reactive value updates as OTel log events.
**Status**: In Review - PR #2169
- Added `emit_otel_log()` helper function
- Value updates logged with DEBUG severity
- Namespace support for module-scoped values
- 12 comprehensive tests
- Example application

### 6. Error Handling and Sanitization [#2137]
Record exceptions in spans with proper sanitization for sensitive information.
**Status**: Not Started

### 7. User-Facing API [#2138]
Provide context managers and decorators for user control over OTel collection.
**Status**: Not Started

### 8. Testing Infrastructure [#2139]
Add comprehensive tests for OTel functionality with in-memory exporters and fixtures.
**Status**: Not Started (test infrastructure added incrementally in each phase)

### 9. Documentation [#2140]
Document OTel features for users including API docs, user guide, and examples.
**Status**: Not Started

### 10. Follow-up Evaluation [#2141]
Evaluate whether optional dependency group approach is better than required dependency.
**Status**: Not Started

---

See linked sub-issues below for detailed implementation plans for each phase.

---

## Implementation Notes

### Non-Goals (Out of Scope)
- ASGI middleware for automatic HTTP tracing
- Metrics collection (only traces and logs)
- Custom span processors or exporters
- Integration with specific observability platforms
- Automatic instrumentation of third-party libraries

### Open Questions

- [ ] #2185
